title: Automated monitoring Terraform module + rollback-safe Grafana provisioner for private installs
author: Leah Moreno
body: Motivation: Private installs need a reproducible, auditable way to provision Prometheus/Grafana and associate alerting/runbooks that is safe during upgrades and supports rollback. This PR introduces a reusable Terraform module for provisioning monitoring components (CRDs, service accounts, storage options) and a Helm-based Grafana provisioner that stores dashboard manifests in an immutable manifest store so upgrades can be validated and safely rolled back. What this PR does: 1) Terraform module 'monitoring' (modules/monitoring) that supports two modes: managed (installs kube-prometheus-stack via Helm) and external (skips installation, wires secrets/CRDs). 2) Grafana provisioner Helm chart (charts/grafana-provisioner) that accepts a list of dashboard bundles produced by the installer; the provisioner writes dashboard metadata to an S3/GCS-compatible manifest store and exposes a postUpgrade validation job that runs synthetic dashboard queries to detect rendering regressions. 3) Rollback-safe mechanism: every upgrade writes a manifest snapshot and a lightweight pre-upgrade validation token so the post-upgrade hook can compare metrics/dashboards and, on failure, emit a rollback flag consumed by the installer to automatically revert to the previous helm release. 4) Alert runbook generator (tools/alert-runbook-gen) that compiles firing alerts into a templated runbook (Markdown) stored alongside alerts; runbooks are included as annotations on the Alertmanager rules. 5) Integration with KMS-backed secrets for Grafana provisioning (supports AWS KMS + customer-managed keys for Private deployments). 6) CI and e2e tests: added terraform plan validation, helm chart linting, and an integration test that boots a k3s cluster in CI, runs the module in 'managed' mode, deploys a small workload that emits synthetic metrics, and asserts alert firing and dashboard ingestion. Backwards compatibility: module defaults to no-op for clusters which already have Prometheus installed; the provisioner will detect existing Grafana instances and can operate by injecting dashboards via the API instead of replacing the deployment. Rollout plan: staged canary rollout across Private installs with feature flag in installer; initial rollout to internal staging customers followed by a gradual ramp. Security considerations: dashboards and API keys are encrypted via KMS; manifest store supports encryption-at-rest and ACLs; RBAC roles are scoped minimally. Upgrade notes: operators should run the included 'monitoring:validate' command before upgrading critical clusters to capture baseline manifests. Testing: local integration test included (ci/integration/monitoring.sh) and a nightly job in CI that executes a full upgrade+rollback cycle against a k3s cluster. Files changed are small and focused to make reviewable; see changed_files for specifics.
commits_summary: feat(terraform): add modules/monitoring with managed/external modes
feat(helm): add charts/grafana-provisioner with manifest-store support
chore(ci): add terraform validate & helm lint steps to pipeline
test(integration): add ci integration test for upgrade+rollback cycle
docs: add runbook and upgrade notes to docs/private-monitoring.md
review_comments: Marco Chen: I like the manifest snapshot approach. Request: add an immutable timestamped key format to avoid accidental overwrites during parallel upgrades.
Leah Moreno: responded - switched to a UUID+timestamp naming pattern and added tests to ensure parallel upgrades write separate keys.
Priya Singh: Request changes - tighten RBAC in charts/grafana-provisioner to avoid cluster-admin. Also please add explicit minimal PSP/netpol for private clusters.
Leah Moreno: addressed - updated deployment.yaml with least-privilege roles and added a NetworkPolicy sample for private installs.
Arjun Patel: Approved after CI green and one integration run that includes rollback validation. Left a note about adding a telemetry metric for 'provisioner.rollback_count'.
CI Bot: All checks passed (terraform validate, helm lint, unit tests, integration smoke).
tests: Added terraform plan & validate in CI, helm chart linting, unit tests for alert-runbook-gen, and a CI integration job that performs managed-mode install, triggers an alert, validates dashboard rendering, performs an upgrade, and intentionally fails post-upgrade validation to exercise rollback path.
release_notes: New: Terraform monitoring module for Private installs with managed/external modes; Grafana provisioner that snapshots dashboard manifests and supports safe rollback; Alert runbook generator attaches runbooks to alerts; CI integration tests for upgrade+rollback. Notes: default behavior is backward compatible; enable via installer feature flag for staged rollout.
notes_for_ops: To enable in existing private deployments, set installer flag 'enable_monitoring_module=true' and provide either a 'managed' config or point to an external Prometheus. For clusters using KMS, supply kms_key_arn in tfvars. To force a rollback during testing, create a failure marker file referenced by the post-upgrade job. See docs/private-monitoring.md for CLI steps.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: dashboard regressions during upgrades may affect on-call. Mitigation: post-upgrade validation job blocks promotion on rendering/metric mismatches and the installer can automatically revert helm release. Runbooks are autogenerated and included on alerts to speed triage.
changelog_entry: [private-installer] Added monitoring terraform module and grafana provisioner (safe upgrades + rollback), alert runbook generator, and CI upgrade/rollback tests.
upgrade_instructions: Run 'installer apply --target monitoring --validate-only' to capture baseline manifests before upgrading the provisioner. After upgrade run 'installer monitoring:compare --baseline <id> --current <id>' and only mark the rollout as complete when compare returns OK. If compare fails, installer will optionally revert when 'auto_rollback=true' is set.
support_notes: Linked support ticket SUP-811 contains customer repro steps that motivated the rollback automation. On incidents, use the 'manifest-store' to fetch the last known-good dashboard snapshot and redeploy with 'installer dashboard restore --snapshot <id>'.
